To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mutations in the thiol-disulfides oxidoreductases BDBC and BDBD can suppress cytochrome c deficiency of CCDA-defective Bacillus subtlis cells.

B. subtili BdbC and bbdD proteins are thiol-disulphide oxidoreductase that can functionally replace CcdA in the formation of covalent bonds between heme and cysteinyl residues in cytochromes of c-type.

BdbC and DsbD are thiol oxidoreductases that function in the reduction of CcdA, the membrane protein that transfers reducing equivalents to the outer side of cytoplasmic membranes of Bacillus subtils cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which the cysteinyls of the apocytochrome CXXCH motif are reduced in the cytoplamix of B. subtili and the mechanism by which heme covalent bonds are formed.
the synthesis of membrane-anchored cytochromes c and the function of the CcdA and Bdb proteins in the synthesis of cytochromes and spores.
the synthesis of cytochromes in the gram-positive B. subtili.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bdbC gene is a suppressor of ccdA, whereas the bdbD gene is a non-suppressor.
BdbC and DsbB are the same protein and BdbD and DsbA are the same protein.
the BdbC and the BdbD proteins are thiol-disulphide oxidoreductase proteins that are involved in the formation of disulphide bonds of cytochromes of type c.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the B. subtili bdbC and BbdD genes are required for the maturation of cytochromes c and for the synthesis of the spores.
CcdA and the BdbC and D proteins are involved in the reduction of the cysteinyls of the CXXCH heme-binding site in the apocytochrome in the cytoploplasmic membrane.

the BdbC and DsbD proteins are required for cytochrome c synthesis and that the CcdA and DsbA enzymes are involved in transferring reducing equivalents from thiols in the cytoplASM to the BdbC protein, which is required for the synthesis of the disulfide bond in the CXXC motif of cytochrome c.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoplasm of B. subtili is connected with the periplasm of E. coli by a pathway that involves the BdbC and D proteins.
the BdbC and DsbB proteins function in a similar manner, i.e., to transfer electrons from the cytoplasm across the cytoplasmatic membrane to proteins on the periplasm side of the membrane.
the BdbC and the BdbD proteins are required for the maturation of cytochromes of c type.
